Gestionar y dar soporte legal en materia de permisos, derechos mineros, servidumbres y procedimientos administrativos ante autoridades mineras y organismos públicos, identificando riesgos y proponiendo estrategias que permitan avanzar con los proyectos de manera oportuna y jurídicamente segura.

Principales Responsabilidades:

• Asesorar en la interpretación y aplicación del Código de Minería, la normativa minera nacional y provincial, y demás disposiciones legales aplicables a la actividad minera.

• Gestionar y realizar el seguimiento legal de derechos mineros, concesiones, permisos, servidumbres mineras y demás procedimientos administrativos necesarios para el desarrollo de los proyectos.

• Preparar, revisar y coordinar presentaciones, escritos, notas, descargos, recursos y demás actuaciones administrativas ante autoridades mineras y otros organismos públicos.

• Realizar el seguimiento de expedientes administrativos, asegurando el cumplimiento de los requerimientos, plazos y condiciones regulatorias aplicables.

• Identificar y evaluar riesgos legales y regulatorios que puedan afectar el desarrollo, la construcción o la operación de los proyectos, proponiendo medidas de mitigación.

• Analizar los aspectos legales vinculados con el acceso a tierras, las propiedades superficiales, las servidumbres y los derechos necesarios para la ejecución de los proyectos.

• Revisar informes, antecedentes y documentación técnica, asegurando su consistencia con los requerimientos legales y regulatorios aplicables.

• Mantener actualizada la matriz normativa y regulatoria minera, identificando cambios legislativos y regulatorios y evaluando su impacto en el negocio.

• Coordinar, cuando corresponda, el trabajo de asesores legales externos, escribanos y otros especialistas, asegurando la coherencia de sus intervenciones con la estrategia legal de la Compañía.

• Mantener una relación profesional y técnicamente sólida con las autoridades mineras y demás organismos gubernamentales, en coordinación con las áreas correspondientes.

• Contribuir a la elaboración de informes legales, reportes de riesgos, procesos de due diligence y documentación requerida para auditorías, financiamiento y otros procesos corporativos, en materias de su especialidad.

Requisitos:

• Abogado/a. Se valorará contar con especialización o formación de posgrado en Derecho Minero, Derecho Administrativo, Recursos Naturales, Derecho Ambiental o disciplinas relacionadas.

• Experiencia relevante de 7 años en derecho minero y regulatorio; gestión de procedimientos administrativos ante autoridades; participación en proyectos mineros y/o industrias extractivas; gestión de permisos, concesiones, servidumbres, derechos mineros y acceso a tierras; y trabajo con equipos técnicos multidisciplinarios.

• Conocimientos de Código de Minería argentino y normativa complementaria; normativa minera provincial; derecho y procedimientos administrativos; marco legal ambiental aplicable a la actividad minera; régimen de derechos mineros, servidumbres y propiedad superficial; y procesos de permisos y autorizaciones vinculados con proyectos mineros.

• Capacidad de análisis jurídico e interpretación normativa; habilidad para interpretar información técnica y traducirla en implicancias legales y regulatorias; excelente; capacidad de negociación y relacionamiento con autoridades; trabajo interdisciplinario y en equipo; autonomía, criterio profesional y orientación a resultados.

The Attorney Specialist will serve as a trusted legal partner to Procurement professionals primarily located in North America while collaborating with legal and business teams across multiple functions and geographies. Main Responsibilities

• Review, draft, negotiate, and manage a broad range of procurement-related agreements, including supply agreements, services agreements, equipment purchase agreements, subcontracting agreements, logistics and transportation agreements, distribution agreements, technology and SaaS agreements, non-disclosure agreements, contract manufacturing and tolling agreements, quality agreements, statements of work, consulting agreements, and other supplier-facing commercial contracts.

• Review and negotiate supplier-drafted agreements and third-party paper, identifying legal and commercial risks and proposing acceptable alternatives consistent with Ecolab policies.

• Provide day-to-day legal support to Procurement, Supply Chain, and other business stakeholders, primarily supporting North American operations.

• Identify, assess, and communicate legal and commercial risks associated with procurement transactions, including risks relating to indemnification, limitation of liability, warranties, intellectual property, confidentiality, insurance, compliance requirements, and other key contractual terms.

• Support Procurement and business teams in negotiating contract terms that align with Ecolab policies, risk tolerance, and business objectives.

• Provide practical, risk-adjusted legal advice that enables internal clients to make informed business decisions.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with legal and business stakeholders across supported functions and geographies.

• Partner with key stakeholders and Global Capability Owners to understand business priorities and support effective delivery of legal services.

• Utilize contract templates, approved clause libraries, playbooks, and established processes to drive consistency and efficiency in contracting activities.

• Collaborate closely with Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Quality, Supply Chain, Procurement, Finance, Compliance, and other business functions to support effective contracting practices and consistent risk management.

• Support the development and continuous improvement of contract templates, guidance materials, knowledge resources, contracting processes, and training resources.

• Leverage contract lifecycle management tools, workflow solutions, and approved AI-enabled technologies to improve efficiency, consistency, and service delivery.

• Manage multiple matters simultaneously while maintaining high-quality legal work product and responsiveness to business needs.

Requirements

• Law degree and authorization to practice law.

• 5+ years of experience in a law firm, corporate legal department, or a combination of both, with substantial experience in commercial contracting and procurement-related matters.

• Strong experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex commercial agreements.

• Experience supporting Procurement, Supply Chain, manufacturing, logistics, technology, or other commercial business functions.

• Experience working with high tech equipment manufacturing clients or businesses, including those in the computer engineering, AI development, or data center or hyperscaler development or construction industries is preferred.

• Proven experience negotiating commercial agreements, including supplier-facing agreements such as services agreements, supply agreements, technology agreements, logistics agreements, purchase agreements, statements of work, consulting agreements, and other procurement-related contracts.

• Strong ability to identify, assess, and communicate legal and commercial risks in a practical and business-oriented manner.

• Experience advising Procurement and business stakeholders on contractual and commercial risk matters.

• Demonstrated ability to independently manage a high volume of contracts and competing priorities.

• Excellent English verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to draft, review, negotiate, and advise on contracts in English.

• Demonstrated experience working independently in a dynamic and complex environment within a leading law firm or the legal department of a multinational organization.

• Strong legal judgment with a practical approach to problem-solving and risk management.

• Ability to translate complex legal concepts into practical business advice.

• Excellent legal skills combined with strong commercial understanding.

• Positive, proactive, and solution-oriented approach.

• Strong prioritization and project management skills, with the ability to perform under pressure.

• Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with stakeholders across countries and global functions.

• High ethical standards, integrity, and personal accountability.

postings.title: Especialista de Legales y Permisos
postings.descriptionText:
Eramine Sudamérica SA es una subsidiaria de Eramet, un grupo minero y metalúrgico global francés. Está ubicada en el Salar Centenario Ratones, a 3.800 metros sobre el nivel del mar, en el departamento de Los Andes, en la provincia de Salta, Argentina.

Las actividades de exploración tuvieron inicio hace 12 años y a fines de 2019 comenzó a operar nuestra planta piloto que proporciona una demostración de la calidad del producto final de carbonato de litio, con más de un 90% de eficiencia de extracción directa.

Especialista de Legales y Permisos

Descripción

El/la Especialista de Legales y Permisos brinda soporte jurídico especializado a la Gerencia de Legales, especialmente en materia de derecho minero, regulatorio y corporativo (contractual y societario), y lleva a cabo la gestión del sistema de permisos ambientales, mineros y sectoriales del Proyecto Centenario Ratones.

La posición tiene a su cargo el seguimiento de las obligaciones que surgen de la normativa y de los permisos de la compañía, y asegura la actualización diaria de la Matriz Legal y del registro de permisos (permit tracker). Mantiene contacto directo con la Secretaría de Minería y el Juzgado de Minas para la presentación de escritos y el seguimiento de expedientes, y coordina de manera transversal con el área de Medio Ambiente y otros equipos internos y consultores externos para asegurar la obtención, el mantenimiento y el cumplimiento de los distintos permisos.

Esta posición reporta a: Gerente de Legales.

Ubicación: Oficina central en Salta, con viajes eventuales al sitio (Salar Centenario Ratones, +3.800 m.s.n.m.) de acuerdo con los requerimientos operativos y regulatorios del puesto.

Responsabilidades

• Brindar soporte jurídico a la Gerencia de Legales en la dinámica diaria de la compañía, especialmente en temas de derecho minero, contractual y societario.

• Redactar contratos comerciales, convenios y otros instrumentos jurídicos, así como notas y comunicaciones dirigidas a contratistas, proveedores y otros terceros.

• Gestionar, realizar el seguimiento y mantener actualizada la matriz de propiedades mineras.

• Coordinar y mantener actualizada la Matriz Legal, con sus vigencias, condicionantes e hitos críticos.

• Monitorear el cumplimiento de las condiciones establecidas en las Declaraciones de Impacto Ambiental (DIA) y en cada permiso vigente.

• Administrar y mantener actualizado el registro de permisos (permit tracker), con sus condiciones asociadas, plazos y entregables de cumplimiento.

• Coordinar la documentación técnica y legal necesaria para la obtención y el mantenimiento de permisos, junto con equipos técnicos internos y consultores externos.

• Garantizar la disponibilidad de documentación ante auditorías, inspecciones y requerimientos corporativos.

• Recepcionar, registrar y canalizar notificaciones de autoridades, y asistir en la coordinación de respuestas técnicas formales a observaciones, intimaciones o requerimientos, asegurando el cumplimiento de los plazos.

• Mantener trazabilidad completa de todas las comunicaciones regulatorias.

• Articular con las distintas áreas de Eramine el cumplimiento de los permisos, asegurando que cada condición tenga un responsable asignado y evidencia asociada.

• Preparar reportes periódicos de estado para la Dirección de Legales y Compliance.

Su Perfil

• Abogado/a. Se valorará formación relacionada con derecho minero.

• Experiencia mínima de 4 años en departamentos legales de empresas de la industria y/o estudios jurídicos especializados en derecho minero.

• Experiencia en el seguimiento de expedientes judiciales y ante autoridades mineras y ambientales provinciales argentinas.

• Se valorará experiencia en minería de litio, minería metalífera o industria extractiva.

• Experiencia en redacción de contratos y documentos legales.

• Conocimiento sólido del marco regulatorio ambiental y minero argentino: Ley General del Ambiente (25.675), Código de Minería, Ley de Residuos Peligrosos (24.051), Ley de Glaciares (26.639) y normativa provincial de Salta.

• Se valorará conocimiento de ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, IRMA Standard e IFC Performance Standards.

• Pensamiento crítico orientado al cumplimiento regulatorio minero y ambiental, y capacidad de articulación con múltiples áreas y niveles de la organización.

• Alto nivel de orden y sistematización, con capacidad de gestión autónoma de múltiples expedientes con plazos críticos simultáneos.

• Autonomía, integridad y discreción en el manejo de asuntos regulatorios sensibles.

• Español nativo. Inglés intermedio.

Presente en los cinco continentes y con empleados de más de 70 nacionalidades, Eramet es por naturaleza un grupo inherentemente diverso.

Convencidos de que la diversidad es una ventaja, nos comprometemos a acoger a todos los talentos, independientemente de su género, discapacidad, edad, origen social o cultural, orientación sexual y creencias.

Nos comprometemos a ofrecer a todos los empleados el apoyo y las oportunidades de desarrollo que necesitan a lo largo de su carrera profesional.

postings.title: Legal Manager
postings.descriptionText:
Glencore is one of the world’s largest diversified natural resource companies and a leading producer and marketer of more than 60 commodities that make everyday life possible. Through a network of assets, customers, and suppliers spanning the globe, we produce, process, recycle, source, market, and distribute the raw materials that enable decarbonization while meeting today’s energy needs. With around 140,000 employees and contractors and a strong presence in more than 35 countries—across both established and emerging resource regions—our industrial and marketing activities are supported by a global network of more than 40 offices.

Legal Manager - Argentina

Location: Buenos Aires, Argentina

Business Unit: Glencore Servicios Corporativos Argentina S.A.U.

Reports To: CEO Argentina

Dotted Line: Global Head of Legal – Glencore Copper Industrial Assets

Direct Reports: 2

Department: Argentina Country Leadership

Travel Requirements: Regular travel across Argentina, particularly to San Juan and Catamarca, with international travel as required

POSITION PURPOSE

The Legal Manager – Argentina is responsible for leading and coordinating legal support across Glencore’s activities and development portfolio in Argentina, providing strategic, commercially focused legal advice to the CEO Argentina, senior leadership and project teams.

The role provides legal leadership across a broad range of corporate, regulatory, commercial, governance and project development matters, with a particular focus on supporting the advancement of MARA in Catamarca and El Pachón in San Juan.

Working closely with the CEO Argentina and maintaining a functional relationship with the Global Head of Legal – Glencore Copper Industrial Assets, the Legal Manager ensures that material legal risks are identified, understood and effectively managed and reported, and that the Argentina organisation has access to high-quality legal advice to support business and investment decisions.

The position requires a senior legal professional capable of combining strong technical expertise with commercial judgement and operating effectively across major projects, multiple jurisdictions and a complex stakeholder environment.

OPERATING CONTEXT

Glencore has established a dedicated Argentina organisation to shape and advance its significant investment and development portfolio in the country, currently centred on the development of MARA and El Pachón, two major copper projects located in Catamarca and San Juan respectively.

The Legal Manager operates across this Argentina platform, supporting both country-level activities and project-specific requirements and working closely with project leadership and relevant corporate and functional teams.

The legal environment is broad and complex, encompassing corporate and commercial law, mining and regulatory frameworks, major project development, permitting, contractual arrangements, governance, investment frameworks and interactions with national and provincial authorities.

The position operates within a global matrix and requires close collaboration with Argentina leadership, project teams and Glencore legal and specialist functions internationally. The Legal Manager must balance robust management of legal risk with pragmatic, commercially focused advice that enables the responsible advancement of Glencore’s investments in Argentina.

Key Accountabilities

• Lead the provision of legal advice and support across Glencore’s activities and development portfolio in Argentina.

• Act as the principal legal adviser to the CEO Argentina and provide strategic legal counsel to the Argentina leadership team.

• Provide legal support to the development of MARA and El Pachón, working closely with project leadership and relevant functional teams on material project-related matters.

• Advise on legal and regulatory matters affecting the development, permitting, financing, construction and future operation of major mining projects.

• Monitor developments in Argentina’s legal, mining, regulatory and investment frameworks and assess their potential implications for Glencore and its projects.

• Provide legal advice on the application and implementation of relevant investment frameworks and incentives affecting major capital investments in Argentina.

• Lead and coordinate material corporate, commercial and contractual matters, including the negotiation and review of significant agreements and strategic arrangements.

• Support commercial transactions, partnerships and other arrangements associated with the development of Glencore’s Argentina portfolio.

• Provide legal oversight and support in relation to corporate structures, legal entities and governance arrangements across Argentina.

• Ensure appropriate corporate governance and statutory requirements are maintained across relevant Glencore entities.

• Identify, assess and manage material legal risks and ensure appropriate escalation to the CEO Argentina, Global Legal and relevant governance forums.

• Provide legal support on significant regulatory, administrative, disputes and litigation matters and coordinate appropriate strategies where required.

• Support engagement with national, provincial and local government authorities and regulators on matters requiring legal or regulatory expertise.

• Work closely with Corporate Affairs and other relevant functions to ensure external engagement is supported by appropriate legal analysis and advice.

• Provide legal input into key investment, project and business decisions, ensuring legal implications and risks are clearly understood by decision makers.

• Maintain effective connectivity with the Global Head of Legal – Glencore Copper Industrial Assets and other Glencore legal teams, ensuring alignment with Group legal standards, governance and risk-management requirements.

• Coordinate specialist legal support from Glencore Group and global functional teams where required.

• Select, instruct and manage external legal counsel and other specialist advisers, ensuring appropriate quality, cost effectiveness and accountability.

• Support the development and implementation of appropriate legal policies, processes, controls and governance frameworks across the Argentina organisation.

• Partner effectively with Finance, Tax, Human Capital, Corporate Affairs, Sustainability, Risk, Commercial, Procurement and project teams on matters requiring legal input.

• Promote proactive legal risk management and strengthen legal awareness across the organisation.

• Lead, develop and provide direction to two direct reports, establishing clear priorities, accountabilities and development plans.

• Champion Glencore’s Values, Code of Conduct and expected standards of integrity and responsible business conduct.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS

Internal

• CEO Argentina

• Global Head of Legal – Glencore Copper Industrial Assets

• Argentina Leadership Team

• MARA Project Leadership

• El Pachón Project Leadership

• Glencore Group and functional Legal teams

• Corporate Affairs

• Finance & Tax

• Human Capital

• Sustainability & HSEC

• Risk & Compliance

• Commercial

• Procurement & Supply Chain

• Major Projects and project functions

External

• External legal counsel and specialist advisers

• National and provincial regulatory authorities

• Mining authorities

• Relevant government agencies

• Strategic partners and counterparties

• Joint venture and commercial partners

• Other legal and institutional stakeholders relevant to Glencore’s activities in Argentina

SUCCESS MEASURES

• High-quality, timely and commercially pragmatic legal advice to the CEO Argentina, senior leadership and project teams.

• Effective legal support to the continued advancement of MARA and El Pachón.

• Early identification and effective management of material legal and regulatory risks.

• Strong governance and legal compliance across Glencore’s Argentine entities and activities.

• Effective management of significant contracts, transactions, regulatory matters and disputes.

• Clear and effective coordination between Argentina and relevant Glencore global legal teams.

• Strong relationships with project leadership, corporate functions and external legal and regulatory stakeholders.

• Cost efficient management and value delivery from external legal advisers.

• Development of strong internal legal capability and effective leadership of the Argentina Legal team.

Experience And Qualifications

Core Experience

• 15+ years of relevant legal experience, including substantial experience in senior in-house and/or private practice roles.

• Significant experience practising or operating within the Argentine legal and regulatory environment.

• Strong experience within mining, natural resources, energy, infrastructure, major projects or another highly regulated and capital-intensive sector.

• Experience advising senior executives on complex, commercially significant and strategically sensitive legal matters.

• Strong corporate, commercial, contractual and regulatory legal experience.

• Experience supporting major capital projects, transactions or significant investment programmes.

• Strong understanding of corporate governance and legal risk management.

• Experience working with government authorities, regulators and external counsel.

• Proven ability to operate effectively within a complex international and matrix organisation.

• Demonstrated people leadership and stakeholder management capability.

Preferred Experience

• Significant legal experience within the mining or metals sector.

• Experience supporting major mining project development in Argentina.

• Knowledge of Argentine mining law, investment frameworks and relevant national and provincial regulatory environments.

• Experience with major project agreements, strategic partnerships, joint ventures and complex commercial arrangements.

• Exposure to legal matters involving both San Juan and Catamarca.

• Experience within a major multinational organisation.

Education And Professional Qualifications

• Law degree from a recognised university.

• Qualified lawyer with eligibility to practise in Argentina.

• Relevant postgraduate qualifications advantageous.

Languages

• Fluent Spanish and English required.

COMPETENCIES

• Strategic Thinking

• Commercial Acumen

• Professional Expertise

• Decision Making

• Change Leadership

• People Leadership

postings.descriptionText:
¿Qué buscamos?
Nos encontramos en la búsqueda de un Administrador de contratos para sumarse a la VP Infraestructura.

¿Cuál será su desafío?
Elaborar junto con el Gerente de Proyectos la estrategia contractual a implementar y mitigar los riesgos que surgen de la Administración contractual de la misma en línea con el nivel de exposición aprobado.

¿Cuáles serán sus principales responsabilidades?

• Liderar junto con los Jefes/Gerentes de Proyectos el análisis de riesgos y la definición de la estrategias de contratación, en las etapas de licitación para garantizar la adecuada transferencia de administración de los riesgos en los contratos adjudicados.

• Definir, junto con los Jefes/Gerentes la asignación y delimitación de responsabilidades contractuales y en la elaboración del pliego (Invitación a Presentar Ofertas), en los aspectos de la estrategia de contratación en las etapas de licitación, a fin de asegurar que en los contratos adjudicados no existen desvíos entre la estrategia de toma de responsabilidades definida, y lo plasmado en los documentos contractuales.

• Garantizar la consistencia entre las condiciones particulares definidas para el pliego, con las condiciones de contratación validadas por SSJJ de YPF, siendo responsable de coordinar la participación de dicho sector corporativo en los casos que por el nivel de exposición y/o riesgo así se requiera a fin de asegurar que los contratos no contengan contradicciones entre los Términos y Condiciones Particulares y las Condiciones validadas por SSJJ YPF.

• Participar en la comunicación a los distintos Stakeholders dentro de la organización de las estrategias contractuales y riesgos identificados, así como de las propuestas de mitigación para asegurar la correcta comunicación de riesgos y acciones de mitigación en los niveles de aprobación requeridos por los proyectos, como, por ejemplo, el Directorio, el Comité de Inversiones Criticas, etc.

• Liderar junto con los Jefes/Gerentes de Proyecto el proceso para la elaboración/modificación de los contratos pro forma que van a regir la relación contractual, y liderar junto con el Jefe de Proyectos la negociación de los Contratos de Servicios, tecnología y Órdenes de Compra de Equipos Mayores, en la etapa de licitación, para garantizar que el nivel de exposición de YPF en los Contratos de Servicios y Órdenes de Compra de Equipos Mayores, no superen los oportunamente definidos y aprobados en las distintas instancias de validación del Proyecto

• Delinear la estrategia para la redacción, revisión y asesoramiento en comunicaciones contractuales del proyecto (cartas contractuales, Órdenes de Servicio, Pedidos de Empresa), a requerimiento, en la etapa de ejecución de contratos y provisiones a fin de garantizar que las Comunicaciones Contractuales no generen compromisos que originen Cambios de Alcance, modifiquen el Contrato y guarden consistencia entre sí.

• Alertar al Jefe de Proyecto sobre los riesgos emergentes de las comunicaciones recibidas/enviadas y en el cumplimiento de compromisos contractuales, en la etapa de ejecución de contratos y provisiones para asegurar que no se generen compromisos extra-contractuales o que impidan el cumplimiento de lo indicado en el contrato.

• Participar en la revisión de Reclamos y Solicitudes de Órdenes de Cambio referidos a los aspectos contractuales estableciendo el mérito de lo reclamos y sus posibles impactos en plazo y costo, contemplado los precedentes para toda la vida del Proyecto. Elaborar los modelos de Cartas Acuerdo, de intención, memorando de entendimiento, Adendas y Órdenes de Cambio, a fin de garantizar que no se generen Reclamos y Solicitudes de Órdenes de Cambio por actividades que forman parte del alcance contractual y Dar respuesta oportuna a los reclamos y solicitudes de proveedores y contratistas.

postings.descriptionText:
Company Description

Join an Award-Winning Personal Injury Law Firm

At The Ward Law Group, our mission is simple:

Changing Lives. One Client at a Time

Recognized as one of the Best Places to Work for consecutive years, we are committed to delivering exceptional legal representation while creating an environment where talented professionals can grow, lead, and make a meaningful impact every day.

We believe our people are our greatest asset. We foster a collaborative, innovative, and high-accountability culture where every team member is empowered to make informed decisions, continuously improve, and deliver exceptional results for our clients. Every role contributes directly to helping injured individuals navigate one of the most challenging times in their lives while supporting the continued growth and success of our firm.

Our Core Values

Faith – We act with integrity, honesty, and purpose in everything we do.

Accountability – We take ownership of our work, our commitments, and the results we deliver.

Leadership – We lead by example, inspire others, embrace continuous improvement, and develop high-performing teams.

Loyalty – We build lasting relationships through trust, respect, and dedication to our clients, teammates, and community.

Service to Our Clients – We are committed to delivering compassionate, responsive, and exceptional service that maximizes every client's opportunity for success.

Service to Our Teammates – We foster a culture of collaboration, respect, support, and shared success where every team member has the opportunity to grow and thrive.

Service to Our Community – We believe in making a positive impact beyond the workplace by serving and strengthening the communities where we live and work.

If you are passionate about helping injured clients, thrive in a fast-paced, results-driven environment, and are committed to delivering exceptional client service while continuously growing your career, we invite you to join The Ward Law Group and help us change lives—one client at a time.

Job Description

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Lien Resolution Team Lead runs the function that determines how much of every settlement actually reaches our clients. You will supervise a team of reductions and lien resolution specialists, personally handle the largest and most complex lien files, and own the metrics that measure our performance — aggregate reduction rate, net-to-client percentage, and time from settlement to disbursement.

This is a negotiation role with a management layer on top. Every dollar your team takes off a medical balance, a hospital lien, or a health plan’s subrogation claim is a dollar that goes to an injured client instead. You will set the standard for how hard those negotiations are pushed, hold the team to it, and step in personally when a provider or plan will not move.

Key Responsibilities

• Post-settlement medical bill and liens

• Lead the team. Supervise, train, and evaluate a team of reductions and lien resolution specialists. Assign files, manage workload distribution, run regular file reviews, and develop the team’s negotiation skills.

• Own the numbers. Track and report aggregate reduction percentage, dollars saved, aging, and settlement-to-disbursement turnaround. Identify where the team is leaving money on the table and fix it.

• Negotiate the hard files. Personally handle high-balance, high-complexity, and escalated reductions where the provider or plan has refused to move at the specialist level.

• Resolve statutory and plan liens. Direct the resolution of Medicare conditional payments and Medicare Secondary Payer obligations, Florida Medicaid (AHCA) claims under Fla. Stat.

• 409.910 including the administrative challenge process, ERISA and self-funded plan reimbursement claims, TRICARE and VA claims, and hospital and provider liens under applicable county ordinances.

• Manage letter of protection balances. Negotiate LOP balances with treating providers and maintain documentation consistent with Fla. Stat.

• 768.0427 disclosure requirements.

• Apply the collateral source framework. Analyze health insurance payments, PIP benefits, and other collateral sources under Fla. Stat.

• 768.76 to establish the correct reimbursement exposure before negotiating.

• Build provider relationships. Establish and maintain working relationships and, where appropriate, standing reduction arrangements with high-volume providers, facilities, and lien resolution vendors.

• Partner with the attorneys. Give trial and pre-suit attorneys accurate, timely lien exposure figures so they can evaluate settlement authority and advise clients on net recovery.

• Protect the client experience. Ensure clients understand their closing statement and that disbursement is accurate, documented, and prompt.

• Improve the process. Standardize templates, escalation paths, and negotiation playbooks; recommend and help implement case management system and workflow improvements.

• Maintain compliance. Ensure every file satisfies trust accounting, Florida Bar, and firm documentation requirements before funds are released.

Remote Engagement Details

• Independent contractor remote position

• 40-hour workweek; schedule confirmed during the interview process.

• Reliable internet, a computer, and a quiet, professional workspace required.

• No employee benefits or paid time off.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

• Minimum of four (4) years of experience in medical lien resolution, reductions, or settlement negotiation at a personal injury firm, lien resolution company, or healthcare recovery vendor.

• Minimum of 5 people managed in past roles (direct or indirect reports)

• Demonstrated track record of negotiating meaningful reductions on medical balances and liens, with the numbers to support it.

• Working knowledge of Medicare Secondary Payer rules and conditional payment resolution.

• Working knowledge of Florida Medicaid third-party recovery and the AHCA lien process.

• Familiarity with ERISA plan reimbursement claims and the practical difference between self-funded and fully insured plans.

• Understanding of Florida PIP and the collateral source framework as it affects reimbursement exposure.

• Strong command of settlement math — gross to net, attorney fees and costs, pro rata allocation, and common fund and made-whole considerations.

• Excellent written and verbal communication; able to be firm with providers and plainspoken with clients.

• Proficiency with legal case management software and spreadsheets.

• Bilingual English/Spanish, spoken and written.

• Paralegal certificate, or a bachelor’s degree in a related field.

• Experience building or refining a reductions workflow from the ground up.

• Familiarity with Medicare Set-Aside considerations in third-party liability settlements.

Additional Information

JOIN OUR TEAM

At The Ward Law Group, every role contributes to changing lives.

If you're looking for an opportunity to grow your litigation career, maximize client recoveries, and work alongside a high-performing legal team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and become part of a team committed to excellence, accountability, and changing lives—one client at a time.

The Ward Law Group is not accepting unsolicited assistance from search firms for this employment opportunity. All resumes submitted by search firms to any employee at The Ward Law Group via-email, the Internet or in any form and/or method without a valid written Statement of Work in place for this position from The Ward Law Group HR/Recruitment will be deemed the sole property of The Ward Law Group. No fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by The Ward Law Group as a result of the referral or through other means.

At The Ward Law Group, we recognize our people are our strength. We are an equal opportunity (M/F/Disability/Veterans) and consider all applications without regard to race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, color, religion, national origin, veteran status, disability, genetic information or any other status protected by applicable law. We value our people, their varying perspectives and are committed to fostering an environment where they can bring their whole selves to work.

In accordance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, employment is contingent upon verification of identity and authorization to work in the United States. All persons hired will be required to complete Form I-9 and provide acceptable documentation as required by law.

Who We Are

The Contract Manager is responsible for the overall management of activities involved in the development/preparation and revision of the company’s contracts/change orders with its sponsors.

Effective negotiation skills.

We love knowing that someone is going to have a better life because of the work we do.

postings.title: Lead, Regulatory Affairs, AMER, Amazon Leo Regulatory
postings.descriptionText:
Description

Amazon Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. This is a unique opportunity to work in the development of a global broadband satellite communication system and make a difference in bridging the digital divide.

The Lead, Regulatory Affairs, Americas (AMER) supports the development and execution of regulatory strategies aligned with business and service availability priorities, and identifies potential regulatory risks that may impact Amazon Leo’s ability to deploy services throughout the region. This role is primarily focused on South America, with potential engagement across the broader Americas as needed. The candidate will work on strategies and mechanisms to mitigate those risks, and engage and maintain liaison with national and regional telecommunications organizations. The Lead, Regulatory Affairs, AMER will contribute to shaping regulations affecting non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) systems, telecommunications service providers, the access to and use of Ka-band band and other frequencies for satellite services, including emerging direct-to-device (D2D) spectrum bands, and other relevant regulations, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders. The ideal candidate will be responsible for educating regulators on satellite and spectrum regulations, telecommunications services, and other issues involved with deploying and maintaining a global satellite broadband service. The ideal candidate will have experience shaping regulatory frameworks for satellite communications systems -- to include space stations, earth stations/gateway stations, customer/user equipment, spectrum, the provision of services (wholesale and retail models), and the regulatory obligations applicable to satellite operators and telecommunications service providers, be familiar with regulatory agencies in the AMER, and be able to assess and, if necessary, recommend improvements to regulatory frameworks in order to optimize Amazon Leo service to customers. The Lead, Regulatory Affairs, AMER will engage cross-functionally with Public Policy, Legal, Business, Public Relations, Engineering and Operations professionals, and collaborate closely with Amazon Leo Regulatory team members supporting Global Licensing, Engineering, Global Service Compliance, Technical Program Management, and Law Enforcement Response and Intercept.

This position may require access to information, technology, or hardware that is subject to export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Employment in this position is contingent upon obtaining any required export licenses or other approvals from the United States government. As such, the successful candidate must be eligible to obtain any necessary export licenses or approvals based on their nationality, citizenship, and any other factors considered by the applicable export control regulations.

Key job responsibilities

• Contribute to shaping national and regional regulations affecting NGSO communications systems, telecommunications service providers, the access to and use of Ka-band band and other frequencies for satellite services, and other relevant regulations, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders.

• Identify potential regulatory risks that may impact Amazon Leo’s ability to deploy services, and propose strategies to mitigate those risks.

• Support alignment with Amazon Leo business, technical, and customer objectives to execute on regulatory strategies in countries throughout AMER and enable Amazon Leo services.

• Engage with national and regional telecommunications organizations, while maintaining liaison with regulators, relevant industry actors, and trade associations in the region.

A day in the life

In this role, you will contribute to shaping national and regional regulations affecting NGSO systems, telecommunications service providers, the access to and use of Ka-band band and other frequencies for satellite services, and other relevant regulations, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders. You will support efforts to enable and protect Amazon Leo’s use of radio frequency spectrum and authorization to provide telecommunications services at home and abroad, helping to define and advance the regulatory agenda to allow Amazon Leo service. You will collaborate with trade associations, government agencies, multilateral organizations, and other operators to shape rules and regulations in the best interest of our customers, and work in close collaboration with Amazon Leo business, technical and operations teams to optimize for customer experience, as well as with Amazon’s Public Policy, Public Relations, and Legal teams to enhance the overall regulatory strategy in priority countries. You will work closely with other regulatory country and domain leads and other Amazon Leo teams to ensure alignment on a country and regional basis, anticipating bottlenecks, and communicating risks clearly to leaders. You will take initiative to drive decisions within your scope, escalate effectively, remove blockers, and will deliver results across the AMER region.

You will report to the Senior Lead, Global Regulatory Affairs for Amazon Leo and work in close collaboration with other team members within the Regulatory team and across Amazon Leo to ensure timely service delivery at scale.

About The Team

The Regulatory team enables and protects Amazon Leo’s use of radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbits worldwide, defining and leading the Amazon Leo regulatory agenda to benefit our customers. We operate globally, engaging with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), regional/sub-regional organizations, regulatory authorities, and governments. We obtain the required ITU filings and licenses for Amazon Leo operations, coordinate spectrum use with satellite and terrestrial operators, and shape/promote space safety and sustainability. We advocate for rules and regulations in the best interest of our customers at the national, regional, and ITU treaty level, working with governments, trade associations, and operators. We work with the design, operational, and business teams to promote alignment between business objectives, the Amazon Leo Program of Record, and regulatory requirements and delivery. We partner with the Legal, Public Policy and Public Relations teams to execute the regulatory strategy.

Basic Qualifications

• Speak, write, and read fluently in English

• 5+ years of regulatory frameworks and policy analysis methodologies experience

• Bachelor's degree in relevant discipline (e.g., telecommunications, international relations, or engineering)

• 5+ years of experience in shaping national, regional, and international regulations for the provision of communications services

• Experience with satellite and/or telecommunications networks, and familiarity with the regulatory obligations applicable to telecommunications service providers

• Demonstrated ability to manage complex regulatory issues and drive them to resolution

• Strong analytical, problem solving and communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in working directly with government officials and regulatory bodies

• Experience in ownership of projects and communicating timelines and executing independently

• Ability to interpret technical analysis, and assess impact on operations and business requirements.

• Knowledge of domestic regulatory frameworks applicable to satellite systems in countries throughout the region and experience in ITU regulations related to satellite communications systems

• Knowledge of the regulatory obligations applicable to telecommunications service providers across areas including but not limited to: network security and resilience, foreign ownership, universal service, law enforcement response and intercept, consumer protection, regulatory and spectrum fees, quality of service standards, revenue reporting, and other compliance and reporting requirements

• Proficiency in Spanish and Portuguese, with experience engaging regulators and stakeholders in those languages

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. JPMorganChase is a leader in digital banking and technology. You can play a significant part in key JPMorganChase initiatives by providing first-class legal support to our digital product teams. We're looking for a new member to join our team, where you'll focus on supporting innovative approaches to digital products, customer identity and authentication, and the overall digital customer experience, including the prevention of fraud and scams. You'll provide trusted advice and legal support for new product developments and enhancements, keep informed of and advise our clients on emerging and changes in laws and regulations, provide, data use guidance, and more. You'll develop and further your expertise in laws surrounding digital products, digital identification and credentials, and authentication standards. And you'll do so while working with extremely smart, collegial, and fun business partners and legal colleagues.

Job Summary

As an attorney on our Digital Products & Experience Legal Team for JPMorganChase's Consumer & Community Bank (CCB), you will be able to provide legal support including direct product counsel, advice on strategy and business decisions, conduct content reviews for customer-facing material, provide guidance on data use and emerging laws and regulations, and work to revise as needed our customer agreements and terms and conditions. You'll join a team of lawyers and legal professionals who combine deep product expertise with knowledge of emerging and wholly new technologies and their use for our customers' benefit, helping to drive fast, safe, innovation. If you are intellectually curious, passionate about developing new products and helping to keep customers safe, all while working in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment, let us hear from you.

The position will be located in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Job Responsibilities

• Provide practical, risk-based legal guidance for digital products and services; identification; customer authentication; and fraud and scam prevention.

• Advise on product development, strategy, current and changing legal frameworks, and risk decisions for new and evolving use cases and capabilities.

• Work with senior counsel and business teams on discrete, but expanding, areas across CCB's range of digital products, including advice on pertinent regulations, implementation strategy, contracts, and customer communications.

• Support initiatives involving emerging technologies and partner-enabled capabilities, including governance approvals and issue escalation.

• Review customer-facing content to ensure clear, accurate, and compliant disclosures and communications.

• Draft and update agreements, disclosures, and terms and conditions to support product development and ongoing operations.

• Monitor laws, regulations, enforcement trends, and industry standards impacting covered products and services.

• Identify legal and regulatory issues early and escalate material risks with clear options and recommendations.

• Summarize regulatory developments for stakeholders and translate requirements into actionable product and process changes.

• Contribute to the development and maintenance of applicable policies, procedures, and controls.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

• Lawyer qualified to practice in the location where the position is based.

• At least 3 years of relevant legal experience in a law firm or in-house legal department.

• Background in financial services regulation or supporting another highly regulated business.

• Proactive problem-solver who is not afraid to explore new technologies and can demonstrate a thoughtful approach to testing and incorporating new tools into a professional environment.

• Excellent legal research and writing skills, with the ability to summarize legal and regulatory developments clearly and concisely for distribution and oral presentation to a non-legal audience.

• Ability to develop strong relationships with the business, corporate functions, and fellow legal and support professionals.

• A true self-starter with the ability to work independently to manage competing and changing priorities and coordinate among a wide range of internal stakeholders.

• Comfort in a rapidly changing business environment, and ease in switching subject matters throughout the day.

• Detail oriented with strong organizational and project management skills.

All candidates for roles in the Legal department must successfully complete a conflicts of interest clearance review prior to commencement of employment.

J.P. Morgan is a global leader in financial services, providing strategic advice and products to the world's most prominent corporations, governments, wealthy individuals and institutional investors. Our first-class business in a first-class way approach to serving clients drives everything we do. We strive to build trusted, long-term partnerships to help our clients achieve their business objectives.

Job Description

The Office of the Secretary (“OTS”) promotes effective governance across JPMorganChase's branches, subsidiaries, and affiliates, and works closely with the Board of Directors and senior stakeholders. OTS is seeking an attorney to join the Subsidiary Corporate Governance Team (Americas) , based in Buenos Aires (Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires), Argentina , supporting corporate governance legal, regulatory, and internal policy requirements for Brazilian subsidiaries . The Drive the Future Program is designed to provide university students with their first professional experience while completing their studies.

During journey in our program, you'll collaborate with our expert professionals to influence and shape decisions and initiatives that support our businesses across the firm. In Argentina, DTF Opportunities are open to students from all universities in Buenos Aires. postings.descriptionText:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Join Us as a Sr Site Contract Specialist

Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, our Clinical Research team supports leading pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and emerging biopharma companies in advancing innovative therapies worldwide. Having contributed to thousands of clinical trials across more than 100 countries, we are committed to accelerating research that improves patient lives.

As a Senior Site Contract Specialist, you will play a critical role in the successful start-up and execution of clinical trials by leading site contract and budget negotiations. Working closely with investigative sites, sponsors, legal teams, and internal stakeholders, you will help ensure efficient contract execution while balancing compliance, risk management, and study timelines.

Position Summary

The Senior Site Contract Specialist is responsible for drafting, reviewing, negotiating, and finalizing clinical trial agreements and investigator budgets in accordance with company, client, and local requirements. This role serves as a key partner in the site activation process, ensuring contractual activities are completed efficiently while identifying and mitigating legal, financial, and operational risks. The position requires strong negotiation skills, attention to detail, and the ability to collaborate across multiple functions to support study start-up objectives.

Key Responsibilities:

• Draft, review, negotiate, and finalize agreements with investigative sites in accordance with local regulations, company policies, and client requirements.

• Lead investigators grant and budget negotiations within approved parameters and escalation pathways.

• Ensure compliance with contractual processes, negotiation guidelines, approval requirements, and client expectations.

• Assess and escalate legal, financial, and operational risks as appropriate.

• Provide recommendations and alternative solutions to facilitate contract negotiations and issue resolution.

• Collaborate with internal stakeholders to align contractual activities with site activation timelines and study objectives.

• Support achievement of study start-up and site activation milestones through efficient contract execution.

• Ensure adherence to budgetary guidance, templates, and contractual standards.

• Maintain accurate documentation and tracking of contractual activities within company systems.

• Facilitate effective communication among study sites, sponsors, legal teams, and operational stakeholders.

• Support continuous process improvement initiatives and promote best practices in contract management.

• Ensure contractual risks and outstanding issues are proactively identified, reviewed, and managed.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience.

• Understanding of clinical research, site activation processes, and contract management principles.

Experience:

• Relevant experience in contract negotiation, site contracting, clinical operations, legal support, or related functions within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, or healthcare environment.

• Candidates will be considered based on their experience, qualifications, and demonstrated expertise in clinical trial agreements, budget negotiations, and risk assessment.

Preferred Skills & Competencies:

• Understanding of contract law principles and regulations impacting clinical trial agreements.

• Knowledge of investigator grant and budget negotiation processes.

• Understanding of business, financial, and operational considerations related to clinical research contracts.

• Strong negotiation, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• Excellent attention to detail and risk assessment capabilities.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills in English.

• Strong organizational and time management skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a dynamic environment.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively across cross-functional teams.

• Customer-focused approach to communication, issue resolution, and stakeholder management.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and contract management systems.

Working Conditions & Environment

Work is performed in an office and/or home-based environment with exposure to standard office equipment and technology.

May collaborate with global teams across multiple time zones.

postings.title: Senior Case Manager
postings.descriptionText:
Company Description

Join an Award-Winning Personal Injury Law Firm

At The Ward Law Group, Our Mission Is Simple

Changing Lives. One Client at a Time

Recognized as one of the Best Places to Work for consecutive years, we are committed to delivering exceptional legal representation while creating an environment where talented professionals can grow, lead, and make a meaningful impact every day.

We believe our people are our greatest asset. We foster a collaborative, innovative, and high-accountability culture where every team member is empowered to make informed decisions, continuously improve, and deliver exceptional results for our clients. Every role contributes directly to helping injured individuals navigate one of the most challenging times in their lives while supporting the continued growth and success of our firm.

Our Core Values

Faith – We act with integrity, honesty, and purpose in everything we do.

Accountability – We take ownership of our work, our commitments, and the results we deliver.

Leadership – We lead by example, inspire others, embrace continuous improvement, and develop high-performing teams.

Loyalty – We build lasting relationships through trust, respect, and dedication to our clients, teammates, and community.

Service to Our Clients – We are committed to delivering compassionate, responsive, and exceptional service that maximizes every client's opportunity for success.

Service to Our Teammates – We foster a culture of collaboration, respect, support, and shared success where every team member has the opportunity to grow and thrive.

Service to Our Community – We believe in making a positive impact beyond the workplace by serving and strengthening the communities where we live and work.

If you are passionate about helping injured clients, thrive in a fast-paced, results-driven environment, and are committed to delivering exceptional client service while continuously growing your career, we invite you to join The Ward Law Group and help us change lives—one client at a time.

Please submit your resume in English.

Job Description

The Senior Case Manager possesses extensive knowledge and understanding of personal injury. They assist attorneys with claim handling and negotiations, maintain contact with clients, and provide them with updates on case status.

Essential Functions

Client Communication

• Contact clients within 24 hours of receiving their case to introduce themselves.

• Present initial settlement offers to clients within 48 hours of receipt.

• Educate clients about further medical treatments such as injections, rhizotomies, surgeries, TBI treatment, etc.

• Inform clients about the necessity to file lawsuits.

• Return all client calls the same day.

• Maintain bi-weekly communication with clients to ensure effective communication.

• Inform clients of case settlements and explain the reductions process.

Insurance Communication

• Follow up with insurance companies within 10 days after a settlement demand is sent and continue timely follow-ups until a response is received.

• Communicate settlement offers and counteroffers under the direct supervision of an attorney.

• Conduct settlement negotiations under the direct supervision of an attorney.

• Confirm coverage information (UM, PIP, and BI coverages).

• Follow up on Declaration pages from PIP, BI, UM, and UM Rejection forms if applicable.

• Send UM subrogation waivers and follow up to confirm UM subrogation is waived.

• Schedule mediations.

• Prepare mediation/global settlement/settlement conference summaries or presentations.

File Notation

• Log initial offers within 24 hours of receipt.

• Maintain thorough and accurate notes/records in Litify.

• Keep client files updated in Litify.

• Track offers, demands, and client authority in the negotiation link.

• Save documents or photos in the appropriate folder.

• Enter case resolution details in the resolution link.

• Pay outstanding invoices and keep the expenses link updated.

• Review and update links for injuries and treatment, approval requests, liens, Litify notes, litigations, negotiations, requests, resolutions, etc.

• Use appropriate call subjects when logging calls.

Case Review

• Review settlement offers before sending them to insurance companies.

• Revise surgical case reviews before clients undergo procedures.

• Conduct weekly audits for all cases.

• Discharge cases as needed.

• Draft and file lawsuits on behalf of the attorney, when applicable.

• Dismiss lawsuits on behalf of the attorney, when applicable.

Provider Communication

• Obtain estimates from providers before closing cases.

• Follow up and obtain health insurance liens.

• Check provider balances and obtain POD leader authority before settling cases with hospitals.

Client Service

• Ensure high standards of client service and satisfaction.

• Address client concerns and inquiries promptly and professionally.

• Contact clients every 14 days.

• Return client voicemails the same day.

Qualifications

Required Skills/Abilities:

• Strong organizational and leadership skills.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities.

• Proficiency in Litify software and Microsoft Office Suite.

• Must be fluent in English and Spanish.

• Must consistently be on time and reliable.

• Must work well in a team environment.

• Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to successfully communicate with other employees.

Education And Experience

• Prior case-management/personal-injury experience preferred.

Physical Requirements

• Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

• Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times.

• Must be able to access and navigate each department at the organization’s facilities.

Caseload & Performance Requirements

• Possess expert knowledge and understanding of the complete Bodily Injury Claims process.

• Manage an average caseload of 80–120 Personal Injury cases.

• Achieve a minimum settlements target of per month.

• Meet a minimum requirement of 3 surgeries, 5 rhizotomies, and 5 injections per month for additional treatments.

• Review all settlement offers, additional demands, and surgery reviews within 48 hours of receipt.

Additional Training Requirements

• Required to attend additional in-person training, which may occasionally be scheduled on weekends, including Saturdays and Sundays. Employees will be given 30-day notice prior to scheduled training to make arrangements to attend in person.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Additional Information

Technical Requirements

Contractors supply their own equipment and workspace. Your setup must meet these minimums:

Computer — capable of running a browser-based ATS, video conferencing, and a softphone simultaneously without degradation:

• Windows: Windows 11, Intel i5 (8th generation or newer) or equivalent, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD

• Mac: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel i5, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD

• The device must be used solely by you — not shared with family or household members

Internet — Wired Ethernet Preferred, 5 GHz Wi-Fi Acceptable

• 30 Mbps download / 15 Mbps upload minimum

• Latency under 100 ms

• Private, password-protected network. Public Wi-Fi is not permitted for this work.

Peripherals

• USB noise-cancelling headset with microphone

• Webcam capable of clear video for scheduled calls

Security — Required For Handling Confidential Applicant Information

• Full-disk encryption enabled (BitLocker or FileVault)

• Automatic security updates enabled for operating system and browser

• Screen lock after no more than 10 minutes idle

• Active endpoint protection software

• Applicant data stored only in firm-designated systems — never on personal cloud storage or local drives

Additional Information

Contractor Terms

• This is an independent contractor engagement, not employment.

• No paid time off, healthcare, retirement, or other employee benefits are provided.

• You will supply your own equipment, software, internet connection, and workspace.

The Ward Law Group does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

The Ward Law Group is not accepting unsolicited assistance from search firms for this employment opportunity. All resumes submitted by search firms to any employee at The Ward Law Group via-email, the Internet or in any form and/or method without a valid written Statement of Work in place for this position from The Ward Law Group HR/Recruitment will be deemed the sole property of The Ward Law Group. No fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by The Ward Law Group as a result of the referral or through other means.

About The Project

As a Data Privacy Specialist (OneTrust / DSAR)  , you will play a pivotal role in designing, building, and maintaining robust data architectures that ensure compliance with global privacy regulations (such as GDPR and CCPA). You will specialize in integrating OneTrust across diverse data environments to automate Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) workflows, data mapping, and consent management. Working closely with Data Governance, Legal, and Security teams, you will optimize privacy workflows, implement secure data ingestion pipelines, and build reliable automation to streamline data discovery and fulfillment across cloud and on-premise ecosystems.

What   you’ll   do

• Operate OneTrust to resolve data subject requests (DSARs) end-to-end.

• Execute and follow up on the various compliance use cases related to data privacy.

• Maintain and act on the data map / data inventory already built from the initial scan.

• Collaborate with the data team to build automations between OneTrust and internal data sources (DynamoDB, Aurora, S3, Google Drive).

• Ensure GDPR compliance across Client’s internal databases.

• Serve as the functional point of reference for OneTrust within the compliance team.

What makes you a great fit   🎯

• Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

• Experience using OneTrust to resolve data subject requests (DSARs) end-to-end.

• Experience with ETLs, SQL, comfortable reading data structures, writing queries, and building automations.

• Knowledge of data privacy regulations. Primarily GDPR. Knowledge of other privacy regulations (LGPD, CCPA) is a plus.

• Dynamic and autonomous person, comfortable operating with a scope that isn't fully defined yet.

• Advanced English Level is required for this role, as you will work with US clients. Effective communication in English is essential to deliver the best solutions to our clients and expand your horizons. 

Global Impact, Local Culture   🌍

For over 25 years, we’ve been shaping digital transformation, delivering complex solutions for global enterprises and public sector organizations. Today, we are at the forefront of an AI-driven transformation era, helping organizations turn data into real business value. By combining deep domain expertise with data and AI, we design solutions that create immediate impact while scaling for the future.  

We believe complexity doesn’t have to mean complicated, and that the best solutions are those that work in the real world, not just on paper. That’s why our clients trust us with their most ambitious, business-critical initiatives. 

Apply now and   let’s   shape the future of technology together!  🧑‍💻

Role Summary

The Software and Process Validation engineer is responsible for ensuring that computerized systems, manufacturing processes, equipment, utilities, facilities, and associated quality systems consistently perform as intended and comply with regulatory, quality, and business requirements. This role supports the full validation lifecycle, including planning, risk assessment, qualification, testing, documentation, change management, and maintenance of the validated state.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead software validation for new systems and changes, including requirements, risk assessments, testing, traceability, deviations, reports, integrations, and data migrations.

• Support audits, inspections, and quality investigations

• Perform validation risk assessment utilizing the appropriate risk-validation and CSA principles

• Evaluate data integrity, access controls, audit trails, electronic records and signatures, security, backup and recovery, and continued validated-state requirements.

• Support process and equipment validation, including IQ/OQ/PQ, PPQ, cleaning, utilities, facilities, technology transfer, and new product introduction.

• Apply change control, CAPA, deviation, document-control, and risk-management requirements; monitor milestones, escalate risks, and support audits and inspections.

• Lead validation of GxP computerized systems.

• Develop and execute validation plans.

• Create and review: URS, risk assessments; traceability matrices; test scripts and validation reports.

• Assess data integrity controls, audit trails, electronic records, and electronic signatures.

• Support software implementations, upgrades, integrations, cloud applications, and system changes.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Life Sciences, Quality, or a related technical field.

• At least 3 years of validation, quality engineering, quality systems, software quality, or related experience in a regulated environment.

• Hands-on computerized system validation experience covering requirements, risk assessment, testing, traceability, deviations, and validation reporting.

• Working knowledge of GxP/cGMP, FDA, ISO, data integrity, change control, CAPA, technical writing, and project execution.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience validating enterprise eQMS, laboratory, manufacturing, ERP, cloud/SaaS, reporting, integration, or data-migration solutions.

• Experience with process/product validation, equipment, facilities and utilities qualification, cleaning validation.

• Knowledge of ISO 9001, cGMP, FDA 21 CFR Parts 11, 210, 211, 820, Health Canada, ICH, Pic/s guidance, MHRA Data integrity

• Multilingual communication capability, preferably English plus Spanish or Portuguese, and willingness to travel to manufacturing locations

postings.descriptionText:
Before you apply to a job, select your language preference from the options available at the top right of this page.

Explore your next opportunity at a Fortune Global 500 organization. Envision innovative possibilities, experience our rewarding culture, and work with talented teams that help you become better every day. We know what it takes to lead UPS into tomorrow—people with a unique combination of skill + passion. If you have the qualities and drive to lead yourself or teams, there are roles ready to cultivate your skills and take you to the next level.

Job Description

The Global Systems & Standards Senior communicates the quality policy and objectives to help ensure the maintenance of the overall healthcare compliance for the operation/department. The employee will advise on development of standard operating procedures (SOPs), reviews and approves client and facility work instructions, trains QA personnel and internal clients on SOPs and regulatory topics, and oversees the maintenance of the quality documents. This position participates in internal, client, and agency audits, and follows up on audit outcomes. The HC Quality Assurance Supervisor maintains knowledge of healthcare quality and regulatory requirements: and assesses and addresses risks associated with transporting healthcare and food products. Responsibilities: Monitors and instructs for compliance to UPS SCS site license requirements (DEL, MDEL, CDS, PCR). Promotes Issue resolution, risk management, continuous improvements and project initiatives. Facilitates, hosts, and respond to audits (Internal, Regulatory Agencies and Clients) Assists with creation, revision, and approval of Controlled Documents (SOP/WI/Forms). Provides investigation and Non-conformance reporting, including development of proactive strategies for preventing recurrence. Changes control management. Provides Quality and Regulatory compliance guidance to clients and internal staff. Supports growth of new and expanded facilities, clients and services. Participates in environmental control and CDS security emergency response action team. Performs direct reports responsibilities (risk assessment, task delegation, performance evaluation, skills development, constructive feedback, formal performance review, formal career development) Qualifications: Bachelor's degree or International equivalent in Sciences- Required Pharmaceutical, healthcare or food industry experience - Preferred Quality Assurance experience - Preferred QPIC/AQPIC designation - Preferred

Employee Type

Permanent

UPS is committed to providing a workplace free of discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

postings.title: FSP Country Approval Specialist
postings.descriptionText:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Office

Join Us as a Country Approval Specialist – Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation

We have successfully supported the top 50 pharmaceutical companies and more than 750 biotechs, spanning 2,700 clinical trials across 100+ countries in the last 5 years.

As part of our global team, you’ll have the opportunity to participate in the management and preparation, review, and coordination of Country Submissions in line with the global submission strategy. As a Country Approval Specialist, you'll play a key role in ensuring that submissions are managed effectively and align with our strategic goals.

What You’ll Do:

• Prepares, reviews and coordinates, under guidance, local regulatory submissions (MoH, EC, additional special national local applications if applicable, e.g. gene therapy approvals, viral safety dossiers, import license) in alignment with global submission strategy.

• Provides, under guidance local regulatory strategy advice (MoH &/or EC) to internal clients.

• Provides project specific local SIA services and coordination of these projects.

• May have contact with investigators for submission related activities.

• Key-contact at country level for either Ethical or Regulatory submission-related activities.

• Coordinates, under guidance, with internal functional departments to ensure various site start-up activities are aligned with submissions activities and mutually agreed upon timelines; ensures alignment of submission process for sites and study are aligned to the critical path for site activation.

• Achieves PPD’s target cycle times for site.

• May work with the start-up CRA(s) to prepare the regulatory compliance review packages, as applicable.

• May develop country specific Patient Information Sheet/Informed Consent form documents.

• May assist with grant budgets(s) and payment schedules negotiations with sites.

• Supports the coordination of feasibility activities, as required, in accordance with agreed timelines.

• Entes and maintains trial status information relating to SIA activities onto PPD tracking databases in an accurate and timely manner.

• Ensures the local country study files and filing processes are prepared, set up and maintained as per PPD WPDs or applicable client SOPs.

• Maintains knowledge of and understand PPD SOPs, Client SOPs/directives, and current regulatory guidelines as applicable to services provided.

Education and Experience Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent and relevant formal academic / vocational qualification

• Previous experience that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the job (comparable to 2+ years).

In some cases an equivalency, consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training and/or directly related experience, will be considered sufficient for an individual to meet the requirements of the role.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

• Effective oral and written communication skills

• Excellent interpersonal skills

• Strong attention to detail and quality of documentation

• Good negotiation skills

• Good computer skills and the ability to learn appropriate software

• Good English language and grammar skills

• Basic medical/therapeutic area and medical terminology knowledge

• Ability to work in a team environment or independently, under direction, as required

• Basic organizational and planning skills

• Basic knowledge of all applicable regional / national country regulatory guidelines and EC regulations

Working Conditions and Environment:

• Work is performed in an office/ laboratory and/or a clinical environment.

• Exposure to biological fluids with potential exposure to infectious organisms.

• Exposure to electrical office equipment.

• Personal protective equipment required such as protective eyewear, garments and gloves

postings.title: Quality Engineer - Software & Process Validation
postings.descriptionText:
Role Summary

The Software and Process Validation engineer is responsible for ensuring that computerized systems, manufacturing processes, equipment, utilities, facilities, and associated quality systems consistently perform as intended and comply with regulatory, quality, and business requirements. This role supports the full validation lifecycle, including planning, risk assessment, qualification, testing, documentation, change management, and maintenance of the validated state.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead software validation for new systems and changes, including requirements, risk assessments, testing, traceability, deviations, reports, integrations, and data migrations.

• Support audits, inspections, and quality investigations

• Perform validation risk assessment utilizing the appropriate risk-validation and CSA principles

• Evaluate data integrity, access controls, audit trails, electronic records and signatures, security, backup and recovery, and continued validated-state requirements.

• Support process and equipment validation, including IQ/OQ/PQ, PPQ, cleaning, utilities, facilities, technology transfer, and new product introduction.

• Apply change control, CAPA, deviation, document-control, and risk-management requirements; monitor milestones, escalate risks, and support audits and inspections.

• Lead validation of GxP computerized systems.

• Develop and execute validation plans.

Who We Are

Colgate-Palmolive Company is a global consumer products company operating in over 200 countries specializing in Oral Care, Personal Care, Home Care, Skin Care, and Pet Nutrition. Our products are trusted in more households than any other brand in the world, making us a household name!

Join Colgate-Palmolive, a caring, innovative growth company reimagining a healthier future for people, their pets, and our planet. The Quality Technical Manager leads the quality management system for the San Luis Plant and provides strategic quality support for the Cono Sur region, ensuring full alignment with global Colgate-Palmolive quality standards and local regulatory requirements. • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Microbiology, Biochemistry, or related field
